name: Hairy cell leukemia

meta.title: Hairy cell leukemia in silico decision trainer
meta.condition: Classic hairy cell leukemia, BRAF V600E-positive (adult)
meta.population: Adults; observation for incidental/inactive disease, first-line purine-analog therapy, and the relapse ladder (re-treatment, BRAF-directed therapy). HCL VARIANT (BRAF-wildtype; WHO-HAEM5: splenic B-cell lymphoma/leukemia with prominent nucleoli) is a DIFFERENT disease - the BRAF gate reroutes it out.
meta.summary: Evidence-linked teaching application for classic HCL - the rare leukemia with a one-gene definition (BRAF V600E in essentially all classic cases) and a one-course cure story: a single 5-day cladribine course produces CR in ~90%, and adding concurrent rituximab (CDAR) made 97% MRD-free vs 24% - with 94% vs 12% still MRD-free at 96 months. The disease's real dangers are its edges: profound infection susceptibility around purine-analog nadirs (the consensus guidelines' loudest theme), and the BRAF-wildtype variant masquerading as the same disease. The relapse ladder is timing- and exposure-route…
meta.disclaimer: Synthetic patient. Training only. Not medical advice.
meta.classification: WHO-HAEM5 (2022): classic HCL defined by BRAF V600E; the wildtype 'variant' reclassified as a separate entity
meta.response: Consensus criteria (Grever 2017): CR with/without MRD by IHC/flow; treatment indication by cytopenias/symptoms

stages.label: Presentation & indication
stages.question: Is treatment indicated - or is this incidental disease to observe?
stages.decision: Treat for significant cytopenias or symptoms; observe otherwise (consensus criteria).

stages.label: The BRAF gate
stages.question: Is BRAF V600E present - or is this the variant (a different disease)?
stages.decision: Confirm V600E; wildtype reroutes out - WHO-HAEM5 reclassified the variant as a separate entity.

stages.label: First-line plan
stages.question: Cladribine alone, or with concurrent rituximab - and when?
stages.decision: Rank the purine-analog menu; the CDAR MRD story renders as the labeled surrogate it is.

stages.label: Response depth
stages.question: CR - and is it MRD-free?
stages.decision: MRD after therapy calibrates relapse expectations; it does not trigger re-treatment.

stages.label: Relapse ladder
stages.question: How long did the first remission last - and what has been used?
stages.decision: Late relapse re-treats the purine class; early/refractory disease goes BRAF-directed (vemurafenib + rituximab).

stages.label: Trial matching
stages.question: Which studies fit - including the chemo-free frontline question?

stages.label: Data artifacts
stages.question: Which result moves the plan most?
stages.decision: Rank artifacts by live VOI flips.

Patient.label: Age
Patient.help: A modest modifier; the median HCL patient is in late middle age and does well.
Patient.helpPatient: Age matters little here - this disease's story is mostly a good one at any age.

Patient.label: Performance status (ECOG)
Patient.help: Modifier only - and often driven by the cytopenias the treatment will fix.
Patient.helpPatient: Fatigue from low counts usually improves once treatment works.

Diagnostic gates.label: Treatment indication
Diagnostic gates.help: Consensus indications: significant cytopenias, symptomatic splenomegaly, constitutional symptoms, recurrent infections. Incidental disease with preserved counts is observed.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: If the leukemia is not yet causing trouble, watching closely is the proven plan.

Diagnostic gates.label: BRAF V600E status
Diagnostic gates.help: V600E defines classic HCL. Wildtype means the VARIANT - a different disease per WHO-HAEM5 that responds poorly to purine analogs; it reroutes out (and has its own dedicated trial).
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: One gene test separates the very-treatable classic form from a rarer look-alike that needs a different plan.

Diagnostic gates.label: Active infection status
Diagnostic gates.help: The consensus guidelines' loudest theme: purine analogs cause profound, months-long immunosuppression - an active infection defers the course until controlled.
Diagnostic gates.helpPatient: Any brewing infection gets treated FIRST - the strong medicine briefly disarms your defenses.

On treatment.label: MRD after therapy
On treatment.help: The CDAR-era depth gauge: MRD-free CR predicts very long remission (94% still MRD-free at 96 months with concurrent rituximab). Calibrates follow-up, never triggers re-treatment.
On treatment.helpPatient: The deep test for leftover cells - it forecasts how long this remission should last.

On treatment.label: Relapse timing
On treatment.help: Late relapse (years) re-treats the purine class; early relapse or refractory disease routes to BRAF-directed therapy.
On treatment.helpPatient: How long the first remission lasted picks the next rung of the ladder.

On treatment.label: Prior lines of therapy
On treatment.help: Two-plus lines opens the heavily-pretreated rungs (vemurafenib+rituximab was proven at a median of 3 prior lines; moxetumomab's approval population was >=2).
On treatment.helpPatient: How many treatments came before shapes which proven option is next.

Where you are.label: months since diagnosis
Where you are.help: Twin clock: places 'you are here' on the months-from-diagnosis axis. Not read by the engine (completeness_only).
Where you are.helpPatient: How long since your diagnosis - marks where you are on the modelled journey.

Newly diagnosed.name: Observation (incidental / inactive disease)
Newly diagnosed.patient: Found by accident and not causing trouble: watching is the plan, with treatment held in reserve at full strength.

Newly diagnosed.name: Cladribine single course
Newly diagnosed.guideline: first-line standard for 30 years (consensus; NCCN HCL v2.2026)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: profound months-long immunosuppression after one course - the co-intervention IS the safety program
Newly diagnosed.patient: Five days of treatment, once - and for most people, years of remission follow.

Newly diagnosed.name: Cladribine + concurrent rituximab (CDAR)
Newly diagnosed.guideline: NCCN HCL v2.2026 option; the MRD-era question
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: adds transient thrombocytopenia (59% vs 9%) and infusion logistics to the single-course story
Newly diagnosed.patient: The same five days plus eight antibody infusions - in the trial, nearly everyone's deepest-possible remission, still holding at eight years for 94%.

Newly diagnosed.name: Pentostatin (alternative purine analog)
Newly diagnosed.toxicity: same immunosuppression theme, spread over months
Newly diagnosed.patient: The other proven version of the same cure, given every two weeks over months instead of one intense week.

Newly diagnosed.name: Comfort-focused care
Newly diagnosed.patient: Even untreated, this disease moves in years - stated beside a five-day treatment that usually buys a decade.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Re-treat the purine class (+/- rituximab) - late relapse
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: the same nadir, with somewhat less reserve each round
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: If the first remission lasted years, the same medicine usually buys years again - often with the antibody added this time.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Vemurafenib + rituximab (early relapse / refractory)
Relapsed / recurrent.guideline: the chemo-free answer for the purine-resistant corner (NCCN HCL v2.2026 option)
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: rash, photosensitivity, arthralgia - and notably NOT myelosuppression
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: For disease the classic drug cannot hold: a pill aimed at the disease's one defining mutation, plus the antibody - no chemotherapy, and counts recover instead of crashing.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Moxetumomab pasudotox (anti-CD22 immunotoxin) - WITHDRAWN from market
Relapsed / recurrent.toxicity: HUS / capillary leak 9% each - hydration protocol was the safety program
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: A drug that worked and then left the market anyway - withdrawn for business reasons, not medical ones. It stays on this screen as a lesson and a limited-access option.

Relapsed / recurrent.name: Comfort-focused care
Relapsed / recurrent.patient: Comfort first, in a disease that moves slowly even when it wins.

refs.label: HBV SCREENING (the reactivation law): Hwang et al., 'Hepatitis B Virus Screening and Management for Patients With Cancer Prior to Therapy: ASCO Provisional Clinical Opinion Update' (J Clin Oncol 2020;38:3698-3715 - PMID 32716741, pubmed-eutils abstract read 2026-08-27): ALL patients anticipating systemic anticancer therapy tested with 3 tests (HBsAg, anti-HBc total Ig/IgG, anti-HBs) WITHOUT delaying therapy. Chronic HBV (HBsAg+): antiviral prophylaxis through and >=12 months after therapy. Past HBV (HBsAg-/anti-HBc+) + HIGH-RISK therapy (anti-CD20 antibodies, SCT): prophylaxis during and >=12 months after; monitoring only as an adherence-dependent alternative.

honesty: Unverified statuses never carry the current date; every 'confirm' is in the manifest staleness list - and in a disease this rare, that list is honestly longer than elsewhere.
The BRAF-wildtype result reroutes, never ranks: the variant is a different disease (WHO-HAEM5), and the gate chip links the trial that exists FOR that rerouted population.
The CDAR MRD triumph (97% vs 24%) renders as the surrogate it is - long-term survival equivalence is not yet shown, and the card says so.
The infection gate is the loudest chip in this trainer: active infection defers the purine course, and the nadir vigilance co-intervention renders on every purine card.
Moxetumomab's withdrawal renders plainly as what it was: commercial, not medical - the factory's first market reversal, kept as a teaching case about what 'approved' does and does not promise.
Vemurafenib-alone's 9-month median RFS renders beside the combination's durability - the rituximab partner is the difference, and the card says so.
MRD calibrates follow-up, never triggers re-treatment.
If the trainer disagrees with the paper, trust the paper.
gates: BRAF V600E must be confirmed; wildtype reroutes to the variant pathway (different disease)
treatment arms rank only for consensus-indicated disease; incidental disease observes
